pages.text: In this global context, India displayed steady economic growth. As per the first advance estimates of national accounts, India’s real GDP is estimated to grow by 6.4 per cent in FY25. Growth in the first half of FY25 was supported by agriculture and services.

Although real gross domestic product (GDP)³ growth moderated to 6.5 per cent in 2024-25, India remained the fastest growing major economy. All references to GDP data in this Report are based on the Second Advance Estimates (SAE) of National Income 2024-25 released by the National Statistical Office on February 28, 2025, unless indicated otherwise.

Taking into account these factors, real GDP growth for 2025-26 is projected at 6.5 per cent, with risks evenly balanced. Taking into account these factors, CPI inflation for 2025-26 is projected at 4.0 per cent, with risks evenly balanced.

India’s economy has continued to perform well. Following economic growth of 6.5 percent in FY2024/25, real GDP expanded by 7.8 percent in the first quarter of FY2025/26. Despite external headwinds, growth is expected to remain robust, supported by favorable domestic conditions. Under the baseline assumption of prolonged 50 percent U.S. tariffs, real GDP is projected to grow at 6.6 percent in FY2025/26 before moderating to 6.2 percent in FY2026/27.

relations.explanation: The RBI and IMF reports give the same 6.5% real GDP growth for India in FY2024/25, using the same fiscal period and percentage unit.

Both are forecasts for India's real GDP growth in FY2025/26, but the RBI projects 6.5% and the IMF projects 6.6%. Different publication vintages explain why forecasts may disagree, but the values are not equivalent, so this is a likely contradiction rather than a reconciliation.

The apparent 6.4% versus 6.5% conflict is a data-vintage revision: the Economic Survey cites the First Advance Estimate, while the later RBI report uses the Second Advance Estimate released on February 28, 2025.
